title: Domes
intro: A dome creates a curved covering above an interior space. Look for its ribs, windows and the lantern at its summit.
example: At St. Peter’s, Michelangelo designed the dome; Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana brought it to completion. Its two shells enclose a cavity.
notice: Find the windows around the base.
Notice where the dome meets its supports.

title: Arches
intro: Look for curved and pointed openings around doors and windows. Pointed arches are a characteristic feature of Gothic architecture.
example: In Gothic buildings, arches work alongside vaults and buttresses. Notice how the repeated shapes draw your eye through a building.
notice: Compare the outlines of doors and windows.

source.title: Victoria and Albert Museum — The Gothic style
